title: Global value chains and the innovativeness of firms in Africa
summary: The paper tests whether participation in global value chains is linked to firm innovation in Africa. African GVC firms are highly innovative: they are more likely to introduce new products and processes, to introduce both together, and to introduce radical innovations.
keyFindings: GVC firms are more likely to introduce product, process and radical innovations.
Integrating small, medium and younger firms into GVCs helps them overcome resource constraints and innovate more.
Innovation gains spill over to non-GVC firms in the same industry and region.
methods: Firm-level data from the World Bank Enterprise Surveys for African countries.
